title: Largest Magic Square
summary: Determine the largest k x k grid within an m x n integer grid where every row, column, and both diagonals sum to the same value, allowing for non-distinct integers.
statement: Determine the largest k x k grid within an m x n integer grid where every row, column, and both diagonals sum to the same value, allowing for non-distinct integers. A 1 x 1 grid is inherently a magic square.
constraints: The grid has at most 50 rows and 50 columns.
Cell values are positive and need not be distinct.
Every row, every column, and both main diagonals of the chosen square must share one sum.
hints: Row and column prefix sums make every candidate line sum available in constant time.
Try side lengths from largest downward and compare every row and column with the first row's sum.
Also compute both diagonals; return the first valid size, with size one as the fallback.
Every square is examined at its size, all defining lines are checked, and descending order makes the first success the largest.
editorial: Every square is examined at its size, all defining lines are checked, and descending order makes the first success the largest.

tests.explanation: The largest valid region has side length three.
A 2-by-2 region is magic, but no 3-by-3 region satisfies all required sums.
